title: Domestic Pathways: Where Could Punjab Kings Find Undervalued Talent?
dek: Where is undervalued Indian talent hiding? Low-priced domestic players who became regulars across the IPL show where the market under-priced ability.
excerpt: Across the IPL since 2022, a share of Indian players bought for ₹1 Cr or less became regulars and beat the league average. Punjab Kings have given more such players a regular role than the average franchise.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: The Domestic Market's Blind Spots
body: Every auction leaves capable Indian players at or near their base price. The ones who become regulars and beat the league average are the market's clearest mistakes.

Across the IPL there were {{ev:dp-n}} low-cost Indian regular seasons in 2022–2026 (priced ₹1 Cr or less, at least one hundred and twenty balls). {{ev:dp-pos}} of them finished above the league average on tempo runs.

sections.heading: Where PBKS Stand
body: Punjab Kings account for {{ev:dp-mine}} of those seasons, against an average of {{ev:dp-avg}} per franchise.
They have leaned on low-cost domestic talent more than most.

sections.heading: Where to Look
body: The chart lists the most productive low-cost Indian regulars per ball across the league. Their common thread is a defined role, usually as a specialist in one phase.

sections.heading: What This Cannot See
body: The warehouse holds IPL data only, so domestic-competition performance, the usual scouting signal, is not measured here. The list shows who succeeded after being bought, not who was available.
Players who were bought cheaply and never played are counted in the denominator only when they appear in squad lists.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Buy Roles, Not Reputations
body: Punjab Kings should target low-cost domestic players with a clear specialist role and give them enough balls to prove it.
Adding domestic-competition data would turn this from a record of hits into a scouting tool.
